title: Power-per-token protocol: measurement notes & action plan
linked_artifacts: MLSYS-2026: Green AI workshop notes (local copy)
content:
Quick context and motivation:
I want a lightweight, repeatable protocol for measuring energy (and power) per token across the different inference modes we operate: hosted API (multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem).

Why this matters for Redwood:
- Translate quantization / batching / kernel changes into tangible $ and carbon numbers for customers and internal tradeoffs.
- Surface regressions: a model/setting that looks cheaper per-token but consumes more power under realistic traffic patterns is a problem.
- Fuel Optimizer: hook energy-aware signals into Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Notes from recent readings + talks (quick summaries):
1) "Measuring ML energy consumption at scale" (arXiv 2025) — method: wall-power + per-process attribution via cgroups + sample-based instrumentation on hosts. Key takeaway: per-request attribution is noisy; aggregate distributions over similar request shapes are more reliable.
2) "Thermal throttling and inference latency" (SysConf 2026) — shows steady-power workloads can push GPUs into thermal regimes that change frequency, introducing non-linear latency and energy behavior. Implication: run long-ish traces, not only short bursts.
3) Green AI workshop (MLSys 2026 notes) — recommended carbon-normalized reporting and regional electricity mix metadata; use standardized time windows and server tags.
4) "Power-Profile-Guided Quantization" (EuroSys short) — demonstrates quantization can change power draw profile even when FLOPs drop; memory access patterns matter.

Proposed measurement protocol (first draft):
- Scope: one model variant + one serving config (batch size, kv-cache enabled/disabled, precision, kernel selection).
- Environment labels: deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), region, instance_type, driver_version, cuda/rocm version, thermald settings, ambient temp (if available).
- Inputs: 3 traffic patterns (cold-start single-stream, steady low-concurrency steady-state, bursty multi-client realistic QPS trace). Use our real request traces anonymized (JIRA-ENG-1984) for realistic shapes.
- Duration: warmup: 120s, measurement: 900s for steady-state, 60–180s for burst traces. Rationale: capture thermal/frequency effects and scheduler variability.
- Metrics to collect: wall power (via IPMI / NVML / RAPL where relevant) at 1s resolution, host CPU util, GPU util, GPU frequency, socket temps, memory bandwidth (if available), end-to-end latency p50/p95/p99, tokens generated per second, bytes in/out, per-request token counts.
- Attribution: compute power-per-token = (integral(power - baseline_idle_power) over measurement window) / tokens_generated in window. Baseline_idle_power determined by a short idle probe on same host (30s) prior to run.
- Repeats: 5 runs per config, report median and IQR.
- Reporting: include energy-per-token (Joules/token), power-per-token (Watts/token? better: Joules/token and Watts aggregated), cost-estimate (USD per 1M tokens using cloud spot/on-demand rates), and CO2e estimate using regional grid factor.

Instrumentation/how-to for each deployment mode:
- Hosted: challenge: multi-tenancy and noisy neighbors. Option A: synthetic isolated nodes (spin up dedicated instance in same region with same image) to emulate hosted profile. Option B: run controlled experiments on dedicated test pool reserved for benchmarking (preferred).
- Dedicated: straightforward: pin to GPU, ensure no other workloads, use NVML + ipmi for power. Note: for multi-GPU ephemeral batching, measure at node-level and consider causal token routing impacts.
- Private/on-prem: use IPMI + power meters where available. If we have PDU readings, prefer those for whole-rack attribution.

Experimental ideas to try (short bullets):
- Quantization sweep (fp16 -> int8 -> act-orders): test energy vs quality tradeoff (use our eval sets).
- Batch size and latency SLO frontier: for each SLO target compute cheapest batch setting that keeps p99 under threshold and report Joules/token.
- KV cache & prefix caching: long-session traces where cache hits should reduce compute but increase memory access — measure net energy change.
- Kernel selection policies: try the runtime's kernel choices (fastest vs lowest-power) and see customer-visible cost per token.

Open questions and concerns:
- How to attribute shared infra costs (host networking, NVSwitch) to per-token numbers? For now measure node-level and call it out as conservative.
- Regional grid factors change over time; should we store snapshot metadata per-run and re-compute on a schedule? yes.
- Sampling overhead: NVML polling at 1s is fine for throughput but may miss micro-bursts. Is 1s resolution acceptable? Maybe add 200ms sampling for short bursts.

Immediate action items (first sprint):
- A: Draft a small benchmarking image and benchmark-run script that executes above protocol on a single GPU instance (GPU: A100-80GB) and outputs a JSON summary (JIRA-ENG-1984). Owner: Rafael. ETA: 2026-06-21.
- B: Align with SRE on permissions to run isolated runs in Hosted test pool; create a runbook for safe runs. Owner: Leah Park. ETA: 2026-06-18.
- C: Prototype a visualization in the Redwood Console mock (static) showing Joules/token vs batch size for a sample model; PR to optimize repo. Owner: Tomasz. ETA: 2026-06-28.

Notes to self (scratch fragments):
- Consider showing both Joules/token and kWh/1M tokens — customers like per-million-unit economics.
- For private customers with on-prem PDUs, offer to ingest PDU readings into Console for historical carbon reporting.
- Could integrate as a toggle in Optimize: "energy-aware recommendations" that bias toward lower Joules/token configs when customer has sustainability tag.

References and links I bookmarked:
- Measuring ML energy consumption at scale — https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020
- Thermal throttling paper (SysConf 2026) — local workshop pdf in drive
- Green AI summary (MLSys 2026) — https://doi.org/10.1145/3458817.3476207
- Power-Profile-Guided Quantization — EuroSys short (pdf attached in drive)

Questions for next sync:
- Do we prefer a per-pool standardized baseline (same server hardware) for all published numbers, or publish per-instance-type numbers? Pros/cons for marketing+docs.
- How much integration work for Console to store the per-run energy metadata? Who owns retention policy?

End of draft.

(Will flesh out measurement scripts and add sample outputs once first run completes.)
